default.why: The Raft core is a faithful TypeScript port of etcd's raft: it passes 41 of 41 of etcd's files and 4,000 of 4,000 fuzz scripts (E-10) and was linearizable in 26 of 26 Maelstrom runs (E-46). The share can be reported: etcd's library is about 4,100 code lines, and the host loop around it under 300 (E-10, E-46).

RUST.why: The core is raft-rs, TiKV's production port of etcd's raft, which DEV-04 names. E-10 finds it drifted (it cannot run etcd's 28 interaction files and lacks StepDownOnRemoval, which the row must add), but the core is reused, not written afresh.

EMB-V8.why: The core is raft-rs, TiKV's production port of etcd's raft, which DEV-04 names. E-10 finds it drifted (it cannot run etcd's 28 interaction files and lacks StepDownOnRemoval, which the row must add), but the core is reused, not written afresh.

SIDE.why: The core is raft-rs, TiKV's production port of etcd's raft, which DEV-04 names. E-10 finds it drifted (it cannot run etcd's 28 interaction files and lacks StepDownOnRemoval, which the row must add), but the core is reused, not written afresh.

PD.why: The core is raft-rs, TiKV's production port of etcd's raft, which DEV-04 names. E-10 finds it drifted (it cannot run etcd's 28 interaction files and lacks StepDownOnRemoval, which the row must add), but the core is reused, not written afresh.

SRV.why: Either variant reuses a production core: raft-rs in Rust, or etcd's raft run natively in Go (SPACE footnote 8). E-10 notes raft-rs's gaps, but neither variant writes Raft afresh.

ISR.why: Only #meta's group runs the ported Raft (SPACE footnote 4). The protocol that commits every write (in-sync set, high watermark, leader epochs) is fero's own code from Kafka's KIPs, with no library behind it, so the core of the replication layer is not reused.

SLOG.why: Only the metadata group runs the ported Raft (SPACE footnote 4). The loglets, seals and compare-and-swap chain that order every write are fero's own code from the Corfu and Delos papers, with no library behind them.

OBJ.why: OBJ has no Raft core (axis I is '-'): a commit is a conditional PUT and the writer holds a lease by compare-and-swap, a protocol fero writes itself. The store's conditional write is a primitive, not a consensus library for fero's log.

V4.why: v4 replicates with its own last-writer-wins cells and ballot membership views; it uses no production consensus library (axis I is '-').

BUY.why: The whole log, Raft included, is JetStream's: fero owns 0 lines of that layer (E-44: 164 fero-owned lines, all above the log).

The other estimated rows sit at about 9,100 (V4) and 13,500 (SLOG, RLOG, SPLIT), all within 1.7 times the smallest, and BUY is out by construction, so no estimated row is over 2 times whichever contender passes every MUST, and none needs a written reason.

RLOG.why: E-44 estimates about 13,500 fero-owned lines (82 times BUY) against about 8,000 for the Raft-per-group rows: about 1.7 times, under the 2-times line.

BUY.why: 164 fero-owned lines (E-44), plus the gateways: far below every contender, so far under 2 times.

default.why: One interface, an invariant list and a suite under 30 s per layer, and a CI battery with each repo pinning the other's commit, are build-phase work that no experiment built for any row. The prototypes show such suites can be fast (200 chaos seeds in 0.65 s on E-22's TS prototype, 102 ms with a Rust kernel in WASM, E-04), and nothing in this row's design stops it.
default.closes: Build phase 1: the CI config, the per-layer suites and their timings, and each repo pinning the other's commit.

V4.why: v4 as it is runs one battery of 1,216 tests, and its contract suite pins data's HEAD, not a commit (CLAUDE.md). That misses the pin today, but it is a process gap any build closes, not a failure of the design.
V4.closes: Per-layer suites timed under 30 s, and pins on commits in both repos.

BUY.why: The log layer is JetStream's, so fero can hold its contract only through a suite run against nats-server; nothing built or timed one.
BUY.closes: Build phase 1: a contract suite against JetStream, timed, in CI with the commit pins.

default.why: A kernel of this shape is pure and replays byte for byte: a TS and a Rust twin stayed identical over 1,000 seeds (E-04), 18 recordings of kernel inputs replayed byte for byte (E-42), and etcd's raft is a pure state machine (E-10). But no experiment replayed a sim trace through the L1 spec, and the fold stays identical only with A-10's fold-version pins (E-43: two `data` commits with one SCHEDULE_VERSION differed after 47,994 records).
default.closes: Build phase 1: the determinism canary, and trace validation of sim traces against the L1 TLA+ spec (E-14's and E-15's).

V4.why: v4's kernel is deterministic and replayable by its own design (CLAUDE.md), but v4 has no spec to replay its traces through.
V4.closes: A spec of v4's kernel and trace validation against it (none exists).

BUY.why: (1) DEV-07 needs the replication layer to be pure, events in and effects out, so one seed gives a byte-identical trace. (2) In BUY that layer is nats-server, a separate Go process with its own threads, timers and disk I/O, which fero's simulator cannot run (SPACE 4.2: BUY fails TEST-10 by construction; E-42: no recordable kernel of theirs). (3) So no seed drives it to a byte-identical trace, and no trace of it can be replayed through a spec.

default.why: Bug flow is a working rule for the build: every bug as a tagged failing seed or test, weekly counts in STATUS, and the two stop rules. No row's design decides it and no experiment ran it; a row with a deterministic kernel can turn each kernel bug into a failing seed (DEV-07).
default.closes: The build: weekly bug counts in STATUS from phase 1, with the stop rules applied.

BUY.why: A bug inside JetStream (E-44 found one: a refused publish's message id was kept, losing 58 of 200 increments) can arrive only as a failing test against nats-server, never as a seed; the requirement allows a test, so this is not a failure.
BUY.closes: The build: weekly bug counts in STATUS from phase 1.

V4.why: v4's open bugs went 15, 29, 40 and 34 across October (REQUIREMENTS section 5), the case this rule exists for; whether work stops to re-plan is the process, not the design.
V4.closes: The build: weekly bug counts in STATUS with the stop rules applied.

default.why: The shapes can be fixed in phase 1: slot-shaped positions and cursors need no translation at a move (E-31, E-19), and the experiments list what phase 1 must fix (4,096 slots and delta-coded cursors, A-16; six L0 format rules, E-29; three recorder rules, E-42; five API changes, E-45; the pipelined door, E-40). Whether no later phase changes them can be known only across the build's phases.
default.closes: Build phase 1 fixes these shapes; the interface diff across later phases shows additive changes only.

CELL.why: Its `off` positions keep their shape, but a re-key moves a partition's records to a new generation's log and refuses old cursors (`unknown-log`), which E-31 marks down on DEV-09. The generation part of a cursor (E-17's re-key cursor is generation, cell, index) must be in phase 1's shape.
CELL.closes: Build phase 1 fixes the cursor with its generation part; the diff across phases stays additive.

LANE.why: Its per-lane offsets break at the phase-5 range move unless they carry an epoch and lineage (E-17b; E-31: group offsets break both subscribe modes at the first move, 5 steps). Refusing old cursors at that move, as CELL's re-key does, would keep the shape and move the cost onto P-07, so DEV-09 itself is not shown failed.
LANE.closes: Build phase 1 fixes the lane cursor's shape for the later range move, or the range move refuses old cursors; the diff across phases shows it.

SPLIT.why: `off+lin` positions carry lineage from the start, so a split adds lineage rows, not a new shape (E-17b, E-31), and that lineage is kept for ever.
SPLIT.closes: Build phase 1 fixes the position and lineage shape; the diff across phases stays additive.

BUY.why: Positions, cursors and the record header are JetStream's (stream sequences and its message format): fero can pin a server version, but their shape is not fero's to fix.
BUY.closes: Build phase 1 pins the JetStream version and fero's own interfaces; the diff across phases shows additive changes only.

default.why: The row was counted as DEV-10 says: two counters judged every unit blind (judging/mechanisms.a.json and .b.json), their disagreements are listed and settled by a referee (judging/mechanisms.json; MECHANISMS.md section 4), and the models' rules were found by ablation and their mutants made by script from the model text (E-14c, E-15, E-16, E-17c, E-32 and the others). Two steps differ in letter only: the counters worked from a shared list of 103 units rather than from candidate reports, and the counts are not yet copied into VERDICT.md.
